M1.reason: The outline is off the brief's man. In the side and back views the torso swells into a rounded, pear-shaped blob, with the rear and belly bulging out below the shoulders (sides.png: LEFT, RIGHT, BACK). A lab coat should hang straight from the shoulders. The head is small and boxy on top of it. Height and overall stance are right.

M2.reason: Measured height 68.4 against the brief's 68 (sizeOff 0.007). Width 23.4 and depth 31.6 have no size given in the brief to check against, and both are plausible for a standing man.

M3.reason: Every part the brief names is there. Head with grey hair on top, glasses painted on the face (FRONT), white coat with buttons and pocket flaps, blue shirt and red tie at the neck, two arms with hands, light trousers, two feet with dark shoes. Each part shows at the size the game shows it. The lineup's Valve models all have a head, arms, hands, legs and feet, and the asset has them all.

M4.reason: The coat is white as briefed, but the shoulders and yoke (FRONT, BACK, top of every view) are painted salmon-orange, a region the brief does not ask for and which contradicts the white lab coat. The shirt is blue, the tie red, the trousers light tan and the shoes dark, as the brief wants. The orange yoke is the one clear colour fault.

M5.reason: The coat's buttons, pocket flaps and lapel shading are there in the front view. Glasses read clearly on the face. The surface is plain with soft, blotchy shading, nothing the brief asks for is missing, and no stray marks or smears are visible.

M6.reason: Capped by the line-up test rather than scored by eye. Asked four times which of the four was not made by Valve, the judges picked the asset twice (the asset at D picked D, the asset at C picked C) and missed it twice (the asset at B picked A, the asset at C picked D). Caught twice or more, M6 is at most 1. Beside the lineup's Valve figures, the asset also reads flatter and more cartoonish, with the orange shoulders standing out.

M7.reason: The face and glasses are at the front in the FRONT view, the figure stands upright, and the feet sit on the floor at the origin in the side and back views, with no lean or float.

M8.reason: The SMAK check has no errors (checkErrors empty). Triangles are 1036, under the most Half-Life spends on its kind and size (1640), so the triangle check passes. It is over the three-quarter mark (731), which the kit only warns about. The underside (BELOW) shows the feet and coat closed, with nothing open or floating.

C1.reason: In motion (motion.png, RUN 0/15 to 15/15) the body stays whole: head, torso, arms and legs all move as one, with the arms swinging from the shoulders and the shoes staying on the legs. In the walk (attack.png, SHOOTGUN frames) the arm held forward and the stepping legs also stay attached and move as a body would.
